verses.text: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph. I cried out to God; I cried aloud to God to hear me.

xrefs.text: To the LORD I cry aloud, and He answers me from His holy mountain. Selah
A Psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets.
A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer. I cry aloud to the LORD; I lift my voice to the LORD for mercy.
For the choirmaster. For Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. I said, “I will watch my ways so that I will not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are present.”
For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. In God alone my soul finds rest; my salvation comes from Him.

verses.text: In the day of trouble I sought the Lord; through the night my outstretched hands did not grow weary; my soul refused to be comforted.

xrefs.text: Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me.”
My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dawn. For when Your judgments come upon the earth, the people of the world learn righteousness.
All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said. “I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son.” So his father wept for him.
O LORD, they sought You in their distress; when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.
During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.

verses.text: I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint. Selah

xrefs.text: From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him.
Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.
Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.

verses.text: You have kept my eyes from closing; I am too troubled to speak.

xrefs.text: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping and drench my couch with tears.
Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, but no one spoke a word to him because they saw how intense his suffering was.
For then it would outweigh the sand of the seas— no wonder my words have been rash.
That night sleep escaped the king; so he ordered the Book of Records, the Chronicles, to be brought in and read to him.

verses.text: I considered the days of old, the years long in the past.

xrefs.text: Remember the days of old; consider the years long past. Ask your father, and he will tell you, your elders, and they will inform you.
Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD. Wake up as in days past, as in generations of old. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced through the dragon?
I remember the days of old; I meditate on all Your works; I consider the work of Your hands.
For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah. We have heard with our ears, O God; our fathers have told us the work You did in their days, in the days of old.
Yet God is my King from ancient times, working salvation on the earth.

verses.text: At night I remembered my song; in my heart I mused, and my spirit pondered:

xrefs.text: The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day, and at night His song is with me as a prayer to the God of my life.
Be angry, yet do not sin; on your bed, search your heart and be still. Selah
Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns.
Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.
But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,

verses.text: “Will the Lord spurn us forever and never show His favor again?

xrefs.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. You showed favor to Your land, O LORD; You restored Jacob from captivity.
For the Lord will not cast us off forever.
How long, O LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever? Will Your wrath keep burning like fire?
I ask then, did God reject His people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?

verses.text: Is His loving devotion gone forever? Has His promise failed for all time?

xrefs.text: God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind. Does He speak and not act? Does He promise and not fulfill?
The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.
It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
Why is my pain unending, and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? You have indeed become like a mirage to me— water that is not there.
In keeping with the forty days you spied out the land, you shall bear your guilt forty years— a year for each day — and you will experience My alienation.

verses.text: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?” Selah

xrefs.text: But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!”
O LORD, do not withhold Your mercy from me; Your loving devotion and faithfulness will always guard me.
After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us. But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.
For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.
Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you assert, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God”?

verses.text: So I said, “I am grieved that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”

xrefs.text: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
In my alarm I said, “I am cut off from Your sight!” But You heard my plea for mercy when I called to You for help.
Immediately the boy’s father cried out, “I do believe; help my unbelief!
Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has shattered the enemy.
I considered the days of old, the years long in the past.

verses.text: I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.

xrefs.text: I remember the days of old; I meditate on all Your works; I consider the work of Your hands.
Remember the wonders He has done, His marvels, and the judgments He has pronounced,
Remember the wonders He has done, His marvels, and the judgments He has pronounced,
At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see the work of His hands.
Since they show no regard for the works of the LORD or what His hands have done, He will tear them down and never rebuild them.

verses.text: I will reflect on all You have done and ponder Your mighty deeds.

xrefs.text: My tongue will indeed proclaim Your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm are disgraced and confounded.
They will tell of the glory of Your kingdom and speak of Your might,
Sing to Him, sing praises to Him; tell of all His wonders.
And you shall teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
May my meditation be pleasing to Him, for I rejoice in the LORD.

verses.text: Your way, O God, is holy. What god is so great as our God?

xrefs.text: Who among the gods is like You, O LORD? Who is like You— majestic in holiness, revered with praises, performing wonders?
until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end.
“To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?” asks the Holy One.
To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him?
For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?

verses.text: You are the God who works wonders; You display Your strength among the peoples.

xrefs.text: He delivers and rescues; He performs signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth, for He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions.”
He alone does great wonders. His loving devotion endures forever.
Who among the gods is like You, O LORD? Who is like You— majestic in holiness, revered with praises, performing wonders?
In the future, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you are to tell him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD. Wake up as in days past, as in generations of old. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced through the dragon?

verses.text: With power You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah

xrefs.text: But they are Your people, Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power and outstretched arm.”

Therefore tell the Israelites: ‘I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians and deliver you from their bondage. I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.
In all their distress, He too was afflicted, and the Angel of His Presence saved them. In His love and compassion He redeemed them; He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance— Mount Zion, where You dwell.
And I prayed to the LORD and said, “O Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance, whom You redeemed through Your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

verses.text: The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and swirled; even the depths were shaken.

xrefs.text: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land. So the waters were divided,
You trampled the sea with Your horses, churning the great waters.
Now the Jordan overflows its banks throughout the harvest season. But as soon as the priests carrying the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water’s edge,
The sea observed and fled; the Jordan turned back;
Were You angry at the rivers, O LORD? Was Your wrath against the streams? Did You rage against the sea when You rode on Your horses, on Your chariots of salvation?

verses.text: The clouds poured down water; the skies resounded with thunder; Your arrows flashed back and forth.

xrefs.text: He shot His arrows and scattered the foes; He hurled lightning and routed them.
He shot His arrows and scattered the foes; He hurled lightning and routed them.
to Him who rides upon the highest heavens of old; behold, His mighty voice resounds.
the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the One on Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
O LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the land of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured out rain, and the clouds poured down water.

verses.text: Your thunder resounded in the whirlwind; the lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.

xrefs.text: His lightning illuminates the world; the earth sees and trembles.

Then the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple. And there were flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.
At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth quaked, and the rocks were split.
His radiance was like the sunlight; rays flashed from His hand, where His power is hidden.
Suddenly there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, rolled away the stone, and sat on it.

verses.text: Your path led through the sea, Your way through the mighty waters, but Your footprints were not to be found.

xrefs.text: The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen— the entire army of Pharaoh that had chased the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
The LORD sits enthroned over the flood; the LORD is enthroned as King forever.
You divided the sea before them, and they crossed through it on dry ground. You hurled their pursuers into the depths like a stone into raging waters.
You trampled the sea with Your horses, churning the great waters.
O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!

verses.text: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

xrefs.text: And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.
He led out His people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses. Where is He who brought them through the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is the One who set His Holy Spirit among them,
And the angel of God, who had gone before the camp of Israel, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them,
